descriptor.scene: NO figure, NO head and NO face is anywhere in this picture. The manager is present ONLY as one small mitten stub entering the frame and the plum light it throws; the whole of the rest of him is outside the frame, and there is no lit machine window, port or opening with a figure inside it anywhere in this image. THE CAMERA IS IN CLOSE ON ONE DETAIL. A finished picture book slides out of the open lower mouth of a honey-wood chute and comes to rest on a smooth cream tray, filling most of the frame. The book is closed, small, warmly bound in cloth with a plain cream cover, its pages crisp and new. No lettering, no title, no words and no numbers anywhere on the cover or the page edges. Entering the frame from the RIGHT edge, ONE rounded plum MITTEN STUB, translucent and luminous, rests lightly on the cover to steady it. It is SMALL and in scale with the book, about as wide as the book's spine is thick, and it is a smooth rounded stub with no fingers, no thumb and no hand. It is the only part of any figure in the picture. Plum light spills across the tray from off-frame at the right; warm honeyed afternoon light falls from the chute above. Composition: chute mouth upper left, book and tray filling the centre, the single small mitten stub entering from the right; the lower left stays calm lit tray.
descriptor._caption: By afternoon the book slides out finished: painted, bound, and read aloud in a warm voice. June touched the beginning, when she said what was on her heart, and she will touch the end. The long middle belonged to the factory.
negatives: any face, head, eyes or whole figure in frame

a second arm, a second mitten stub, or any limb at a different scale from the first
an oversized mitten stub larger than the book
fingers, a thumb, a hand or a glove on the mitten stub
a title, lettering or any readable mark on the book
